title: Planned Disruptions Utilized by an Expert Coach in Elite Sport: A Case Study of Ivica Osim From the Perspective of Assistant Coaches
abstract: Planned disruptions are intentional training activities that expose athletes to stress to improve their competitive performance and psychological development; however, knowledge on the types of planned disruptions employed by expert coaches remains limited. This study explored the types of planned disruptions that Ivica Osim, an expert coach, was believed to have used and how their impacts were retrospectively interpreted by five coaches who worked under him. We adopted a pragmatic research paradigm and conducted semistructured interviews with the coaches. A thematic analysis identified four types of planned disruptions—unstable training locations, unsettled competitive conditions, intentional unpredictability, and multidimensional loads. Participants retrospectively described these practices as creating a multifaceted training environment in which players became accustomed to pressure, developed game intelligence, strengthened psychological competencies, and supported team dynamics. Overall, the findings show how planned disruptions were understood to relate to individual- and team-level changes in an elite sport context.
